title: Sigachi Industries Ltd - 543389 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Sigachi Q4 FY26 revenue INR 121.89 crore, EBITDA margin 12.63%; FY27 guidance INR 650-675 crore revenue at 18-20% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 total operating income was INR 121.89 crore with EBITDA of INR 15.4 crore (12.63% margin) and PAT of INR 7.6 crore (6.23% margin), still well below pre-incident margins of 15-20% cited by analysts. Management said operations were stable post the Hyderabad incident, with cellulose-based excipient sales of 14,857 MT at ~82% utilisation. FY27 guidance is revenue of INR 650-675 crore and EBITDA margin of ~18-20%, back-end loaded with H2 higher than H1. The 12,000 MT MCC project at Dahej (INR 106 crore) and the 1,800 MT CCS facility (INR 90 crore) are on track, with MCC COD expected by end-FY27 and CCS commercialisation in Q1 FY28.

segments.name: MCC (cellulose-based excipients)
segments.commentary: Q4 sales 14,857 MT at ~82% capacity utilisation per management; CFO said MCC utilisation ~75-80% as of 31 March. Q4 MCC segment revenue INR 85.33 crore; MCC segment margin ~12.5-13% excluding other income (14.58% including).

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: FY26 API revenue ~INR 60 crore; FY27 expected above INR 100 crore, with API share of revenue rising to ~18-20%. Q4 API revenue INR 17.06 crore. Grandmax API facility utilisation ~65-70%. Management expects API EBITDA margin of 20-plus%.

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 14.63 crore; EBITDA margin ~21-22%, described as a steady and growing contributor.

segments.name: CCS (new excipient)
segments.commentary: 1,800 MT facility at Dahej SEZ; management expects price 2-3x MCC and EBITDA margin above 20%. Expected revenue ~INR 100 crore at full capacity.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance INR 650-675 crore (~35% growth at midpoint, per analyst), EBITDA margin ~18-20%.
H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1; margins to rise from Q1 FY27 and reach 18-20% by year-end.
MCC utilisation targeted at 95-97% per CEO; CFO said >90% this year.
Ramp of new 12,000 MT MCC capacity: Q1 FY28 ~30% utilisation, then 40-50% in Q2 and rising thereafter.
CCS commercialisation expected Q1 FY28; FY29 target of INR 1,000 crore turnover ('not in FY28').
Full normalisation of margins expected by FY27 or mid-FY28.
Hyderabad: no decision until court clears matter; Middle East JV on hold, resumption possibly in ~6 months.
FY28 ~INR 1,000 crore not targeted; management expects it in FY29 or so.
capex_capacity: MCC 12,000 MT per annum at Dahej SEZ: capex ~INR 106 crore, COD expected by end-FY27; takes total cellulose-based excipient capacity to 30,000 MT pa (from ~18,000 MT).
CCS 1,800 MT facility at Dahej SEZ: project cost ~INR 90 crore; some spend in Q1 FY28; commercialisation Q1 FY28.
Land available: ~20 acres at Dahej and ~25 acres at Kurnool.
Funding: internal accruals plus term loan or fresh equity under discussion; no decision announced. Analyst estimated total capex ~INR 200 crore.
Hyderabad facility: not being restarted for now; focus shifted to Dahej.
demand_pricing: Customers described as sticky; during supply disruption some formulators moved volumes to Vendor 2, with expectation of reverting to Vendor 1 once supply normalises.
MCC capacity constraint cited as reason for lost volumes; CCS inquiries received and customers asking for CCS bundled with MCC.
Export turnover ~65% of FY26 revenue across 60+ countries, led by USA, Europe and neighbouring markets; Feb-Mar exports did not happen, so domestic sales were used.
Management said demand exceeds supply and capacity additions will continue as long as demand persists.
Costs: war-related rates increased and production did not rise, compressing margins post incident.

qa_highlights.question: How will FY28 revenue grow once Dahej MCC and CCS capacities are fully online?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects a corresponding revenue increase in FY28 from new capacity plus API and O&M growth; CEO said Q1 FY28 ramp of new MCC will be ~30% utilisation, rising to 40-50% in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 seasonal, and will margins improve from Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said H2 is always higher than H1; Q4 FY26 margin was 13-14%, with margins rising through FY27 to 18-20%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the insurance claim?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the claim is delayed past March; an ad hoc amount is expected around 25-30 June 2026. Fixed-asset and inventory loss claim INR 53.5 crore (INR 49 crore fixed assets plus INR 4.5 crore inventory); business interruption policy INR 25 crore, expected claim INR 16.5 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Has any customer share been lost after the accident?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said some customers moved to Vendor 2 due to supply shortfall; company remains an approved supplier and expects volumes to return once supply is back on track.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt position and credit rating outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said there is no long-term debt, only working-capital debt of ~INR 145 crore per analyst; a later reply cited debt outstanding of ~INR 13 crore for promoter-level borrowing with ~INR 4 crore of shares pledged. Rating was cut after the incident; management hopes for upgrades on better profits.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the Hyderabad facility and any legal exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said full provision has been made, with some reversal expected and no further surprises expected; CEO said restart decision will wait for the court outcome, which is sub judice.

qa_highlights.question: What are the CCS margins and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said CCS prices are 2-3x MCC, with EBITDA margin above 20%, and inquiries are already coming in.

risks_watch: Q4 EBITDA margin of 12.63% against FY27 target of 18-20%; ramp depends on MCC utilisation reaching 90%+ from ~75-82%.
Hyderabad litigation remains sub judice; no restart timeline; management declined to give duration.
Insurance claim settlement timing slipped past March; ad hoc amount expected late June 2026; business-interruption review after 30 June.
Export share fell to ~65% from ~72%; continued dependence on export markets and geopolitical disruption.
Funding plan for capex (~INR 200 crore) still undecided; mix of internal accruals, term loan and equity.
Credit rating downgraded post incident; upgrade depends on sustained profitability.
Middle East JV on hold; resumption timeline ~6 months.
Management ownership: promoter shareholding has declined; stated intention to raise it back toward 48-49%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term volume and capacity recovery, but cautious and sometimes vague on specifics. Management gave firm guidance numbers while deferring on funding mix, Hyderabad restart, JV timing and legal outcomes, often saying "at appropriate time".
key_quotes: Today, the company is operating with stable business continuity, continued customer engagement, and steady progress across its strategic priorities.
we will take the appropriate decision once the matter is cleared by the court.
Now also as of now, as on 31st March, it is around 75-80% only. But going forward, it will increase in this year.

adds.what: 12,000 MT/yr MCC capacity at Dahej SEZ (takes cellulose-based excipient capacity to ~30,000 MT from ~18,000 MT)
1,800 MT CCS facility at Dahej SEZ, expected revenue ~INR 100 crore at full capacity

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR 650-675 crore (~35% growth at midpoint) with 18-20% EBITDA margin, backed by the 12,000 MT MCC capacity (COD end-FY27, Rs 106 cr capex), API revenue above Rs 100 crore and demand exceeding supply, but the ramp is back-end loaded and MCC utilisation is only 75-80%, so backing is partial.
